title: UV Exposure Risk Estimator
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: UV index, perceived brightness and perceived warmth on three separate scales at once, so you can watch them disagree.

learningObjectives: Assess ultraviolet risk for a given time, place and surface.
Justify why the UV index cannot be inferred from how bright or how warm a day feels.
prerequisites: Chapter 9 sections on the solar spectrum

keyQuestions: It is freezing and you are on a snowfield. Do you need sunscreen?
Cloud has cut the light by two thirds. How much has it cut the UV?
Why does altitude raise UV when it lowers the temperature?
commonMisconceptions: Using warmth as a proxy for UV risk.
Believing cloud gives meaningful UV protection.
Assuming you cannot burn below freezing.
assessmentOpportunities: Assesses UV risk from time, place, altitude and surface rather than from appearance.
Explains why cloud is a poor guide to UV.
Identifies snow and altitude as risk multipliers.
